sentences.text: Hulsanpes perlei is a dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur, a group of carnivorous reptiles known for their sickle-shaped claws.
This extinct genus contains only one known species, Hulsanpes perlei, which was named and described by Halszka Osmólska in 1982.
The generic name translates to "foot of Khulsan," combining the Latinized locality name with the Latin word for foot, while the specific name honors the Mongolian paleontologist Altangerel Perle.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is catalogued as ZPAL MgD-I/173 and consists of a partial right foot and a brain fragment.

This foot includes the second, third, and fourth metatarsals, plus the first and partial second phalanx of the second toe, with the longest bone, the third metatarsal, measuring 39 millimeters in length.
The preserved portion of the braincase measures just 1 cm in length, and the roughly textured bones of the holotype indicate it was likely a post-hatchling chick.
The preserved portion of the braincase measures just 1 cm in length, making it an exceptionally small fossil for a dinosaur.
The roughly textured bones of the holotype indicate it was likely a post-hatchling chick, offering a rare glimpse into the early life of this dinosaur.
The longest bone in the preserved foot, the third metatarsal, measures exactly 39 millimeters in length.
Hulsanpes remains were discovered in 1970 at Khulsan in the Gobi Desert during a Polish-Mongolian expedition and were formally described in 1982 by Halszka Osmólska.
Hulsanpes likely spent much of its time in aquatic environments like rivers, swimming using both forelimbs and hindlimbs.

Researchers identified subcursorial adaptations for Hulsanpes, suggesting it may have had a more terrestrial, subcursorial lifestyle despite evidence that it likely spent much of its time in aquatic environments like rivers, swimming using both forelimbs and hindlimbs.
Hulsanpes is classified in the class Reptilia and belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae, with its parent group being Halszkaraptorinae.
In 2017, Hulsanpes was placed in the new clade Halszkaraptorinae alongside Halszkaraptor and Mahakala, representing the first known record of the basal dromaeosaurid subfamily Halszkaraptorinae.

The Halszkaraptorinae is considered the most primitive known dromaeosaurid group, closely related to unenlagiines, a status confirmed in 2018 when Cau and Madzia validated Hulsanpes as the oldest record of the subfamily.

Hulsanpes lived in the Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia approximately 75 to 72 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous, specifically within the Campanian stage from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
The environment of Hulsanpes included large rivers, other water bodies, and prominent dune-like terrains in what is now Asia.
Hulsanpes shared its habitat with dinosaurs including Bagaceratops, Gobipteryx, Parvicursor, Saichania, Tarchia, and Tylocephale.
It was debated whether Hulsanpes belonged to Averaptora incertae sedis due to interpretations of its metatarsals, but later analysis proved those interpretations incorrect.
